name: Arn Autonomy GRID
summary: Small self-driving robot that maps a rebar mat, plans its own route and ties the bar crossings while an operator supervises. Made by a San Francisco start-up and taken on pre-order in the United States.

germany.statusNote: The maker is based in the United States and its page offers pre-order, buy or lease through its own sales team, with a 20% launch discount. No German or EU distributor, CE information or euro price was found.

specs.label: Size (L x W x H)
specs.quote: 3 x 2 x 2.5ftLength x width x height robot dimensions

specs.label: Navigation
specs.value: SLAM and LiDAR sensor fusion with an RGB camera; maps the mat on the first pass
specs.quote: integrating advanced technologies such as sensor fusion, SLAM, and LiDAR

notes: The maker does not describe the running gear, so legs, wheels and tracks are all left false; the pictures show a low box-shaped machine on the rebar mat.
Described as operator-controlled: it ties on its own while an operator supervises.
Safety: perimeter awareness, auto-stop and remote e-stop (maker).
Maker says it works in rain, snow and extreme heat and navigates uneven terrain.
Runtime is the maker's 14+ hours with swappable battery packs; the press release says 14 hours on one charge from a standard outlet.

images.alt: GRID rebar tying robot working on a rebar mat beside crew members on a construction site

evidence.task: Ties rebar crossings on a rebar mat by itself while an operator supervises
evidence.note: Maker press release at the public debut; no customer site is named.

sources.title: Spacer Robotics Unveils GRID: The First Step Toward Autonomous Construction on the Moon

openQuestions: Price: the page says to contact sales for the pre-order and 20% off; no list price is shown.
No customer jobsite is named; the first deployments are not documented.
Running gear (wheels or tracks) and tie wire type are not described.
